sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 reread of the complete original May card and its official PDF. It explicitly names Gemini 3 Flash as its base and architecture reference, not merely a family resemblance. Its model information, benchmark and safety comparisons contain no numerical total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 complete-card reread. The named Gemini 3 Flash base explicitly identifies Gemini 3 Pro as its dependency and architecture reference. Neither model information nor comparisons supply a numerical total or active count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro model card, updated May 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 complete-card reread of the May 2026 revision. Sparse MoE Transformer routing is explicit and Gemini 3.5 Flash appears in the dependent-family list. The original Pro model is not a modification or fine-tune of a previous model. No total, active count, expert size or routing quantity provides a numerical size for this lineage.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact gemini-3.5-flash specifications list 1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens, text/image/video/audio/PDF input, text output, thinking and function calling. The page updated October 12, 2026 says the identifier is deprecated and API requests are routed to Gemini 3.6 Flash. Reopened October 27 for the parameter review: the exact-model specification table supplies no model weight count.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5: frontier intelligence with action
sources.evidence: The dated May 19, 2026 announcement explicitly releases Gemini 3.5 Flash that day across consumer, developer and enterprise products. Direct HTML was successfully fetched after web-reader timeouts. It links the probe paper in s10 as interpretability background. Reopened October 27: the launch post contains no total or activated-parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The hosted service requires acceptance of Google API terms and these additional terms; the terms prohibit extracting or replicating underlying model weights. Together with the model card distribution section this supports proprietary, non-open-weight classification.

sources.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 reread of the complete July 21, 2026 card. It identifies Gemini 3.5 Flash as the base and includes its exact comparison column, but the table gives prices and benchmark results rather than total or activated-parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-card check. The August 13, 2026 model explicitly depends on Gemini 3.6 Flash. Its architecture and complete comparison table supply no retrospective total or active size for Gemini 3.5 Flash.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-card check. The September 2, 2026 model explicitly depends on Gemini 3.7 Flash. Its complete comparison table contains price and capability measurements, not numerical total or activated parameters for the older 3.5 model.

sources.title: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini
sources.evidence: The first-party interpretability paper linked in the 3.5 launch studies Gemini 2.5 Flash; its full text contains no Gemini 3.5 Flash mention. Probe architectures and their sizes are not evidence of 3.5 Flash production-model parameters.

sources.title: A New Era of Discovery: Google Research at I/O 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The May 28, 2026 research account attributes Gemini 3.5 Flash speed to speculative decoding, including block verification and tree-structured drafting. It gives no numerical total or active model size; serving acceleration does not establish a parameter count.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 3.5 Flash record
sources.evidence: The upstream catalog supplies the frozen identifier and gemini-flash grouping; it was followed as a lead and is not the technical verification source.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 check of the complete decoded card. Argon is explicitly a new model rather than a fine-tune of a prior model. Architecture and comparisons supply no retrospective Gemini 3.5 Flash numerical total or active count.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-text exact-name and parameter review found no Gemini 3.5 Flash total or active size. The similar-name monitoring experiments use 3.5 Flash-Lite; parameter references concern task difficulty, weight protection and stored knowledge rather than a numerical model-size table.

sources.title: Developer's guide to Gemini 3.5 Flash
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model search located this current first-party guide, opened October 27. Its exact 3.5 Flash / 3.1 Pro / 3.1 Flash-Lite table lists model IDs, modalities, token limits, thinking and deployment properties without total or activated-parameter sizes. Other parameter references describe API sampling or thinking controls, not learned weights.

name.note: Exact first-party model name and API identifier match.

developer.note: Developed and released by Google DeepMind; Google is the catalog developer label.

family.note: Normalized catalog grouping for the Gemini Flash series; official sources place this release in Gemini 3 and the Flash series.

release_date.note: Dated launch explicitly says Gemini 3.5 Flash is available that day; this is the public 3.5 release, not the earlier Gemini 3 preview or later 3.6 release.

open_weights.note: Distributed as hosted products and APIs under Google terms, without downloadable model weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under Google terms, not the documentation footer license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-name/ID total-size and named-base searches, reopened original cards/API/launch and later Google comparisons found no supported nominal total. The explicit 3.5 Flash to 3 Flash to 3 Pro dependency chain is valid lineage evidence, but no count is published for any named base in the reviewed material. Null reflects absent numerical evidence, not a requirement for an exact tensor census or hosted-service attestation.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-count searches and later first-party comparison-table checks found no numerical active size for this model or its named bases. Sparse expert routing is qualitative, without expert sizes or routing quantities sufficient for a count. Speculative decoding, throughput, thinking controls and benchmark scores are not model parameter counts.

architecture.note: Sparse MoE Transformer through the exact 3.5 Flash architecture section’s explicit reference to Gemini 3 Flash, whose architecture section explicitly references Gemini 3 Pro. This is documented inheritance, not an inference from branding.

context_window.note: Exact documented input-token limit. The separately documented maximum output is 65,536 tokens; these are not summed.

modalities.note: Exact model API table explicitly lists these input formats and text output; no image or audio generation.

reasoning.note: Exact model card identifies a reasoning model, and API table marks thinking supported.

tool_call.note: Exact API table marks function calling supported.

description.value: Gemini Flash model with multimodal input, text output, thinking and function calling.
description.note: Plain summary of documented capabilities for the historical 3.5 release.

patch.notes: Sparse MoE Transformer based on Gemini 3 Flash, whose card names Gemini 3 Pro as its base. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed for this model and its named bases. Specifications describe the May 19, 2026 release; Google now routes API requests using this deprecated identifier to Gemini 3.6 Flash.
patch.description: Gemini Flash model with multimodal input, text output, thinking and function calling.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after independent exact-model searches, reopened original cards/API/launch, the named-base chain, later 3.6/3.7/3.8 and Argon comparisons, the Argon safety report and current Cloud guide. No supported nominal size was found. All unrelated field assessments and corrections are preserved.
